capabilities.name: My Socials (the owner's own social accounts, shown as icons on the public GamID)

contracts.rule: My Socials holds the owner's own accounts on named Wall platforms (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Twitch, Kick, X, Snapchat, Discord, Facebook, Spotify, SoundCloud, Vimeo), at most one link each, added, edited and removed as a draft and saved by the section's Save Changes or Save All Changes. Only account kinds are accepted (a profile, channel, page, Discord personal profile or server invite, Spotify artist, SoundCloud profile, Vimeo profile), never a post, track, playlist, album, episode, show or video. There is no Other option; the Wall keeps its own Other link; Steam stays in Connections. Spotify, SoundCloud and Vimeo were added on 2026-10-12 (9e6e765) and accepted by Mazen on 2026-10-12 (REV-0006).

The Wall's link engine is the only source of platform and URL rules for the Wall and My Socials: the Wall adapters recognise a link and rebuild every address from its validated parts, and the server checks My Socials ids against the Wall's own server rules. My Socials only narrows which Wall platforms and account kinds it offers. Saved content is never copied between the Wall and My Socials.

A saved link is stored as platform, account kind and id, validated by the database against the Wall's server rules, and the owner's list is replaced all-or-nothing; other schemes, hosts, kinds, credentials and markup are refused. Links are reachable only through owner functions acting on the caller's own GamID and an anonymous reader.

Saved links of a published (PUBLIC) GamID appear as labelled icon links leading the public profile panel, also when the owner has no Wall, opening in a new tab without referrer. An unpublished GamID shows none. When a published Wall replaces the profile body, the links are not shown. The Spotify (green), SoundCloud (orange) and Vimeo (blue) icons show their recognisable logos at every width, mobile included (static local marks, 2026-10-12, bc70717, awaiting Mazen's acceptance); on Mobile Public Visitor V2 (public-profile-mobile-v2, ACCEPTED) every platform shows its desktop mark, at an adaptive size.

capabilities.name: Gaming Roles in eight categories, the categorized selector, role badges and Suggest a Role (admin review)

contracts.rule: The ONE Gaming Roles catalog (gaming_role_catalog) holds the 71 roles of the approved list in eight categories, in its order: Gaming & Competitive Play, Streaming & Content Creation, Game Development, Art, Design & Animation, Audio, Video & Production, Esports & Team Management, Community & Marketing, Business & Technology (the owner's instruction says 77; the list it contains has 71 names). Role identifiers are stable keys; the 12 original keys stay (some relabelled, e.g. coach = Gaming Coach) and every existing selection and Primary Role is preserved. Education & Work is unchanged.

In the Profile Editor each category shows its title, description, role count and selected count and expands / collapses; roles are checkboxes, any number across categories. Exactly one selected role is the Primary Role (it moves to another selected role when it is deselected). The selected roles show as removable chips with Clear All. Section saving and unsaved-changes state are preserved. The Account Classic Preview entry point displays saved roles through the existing Classic Profile role badges.
On the Classic Profile the roles show as individual badges, the Primary Role emphasised, wrapping onto further lines; they are never combined into one badge.

Can't find your role? Suggest a Role: a signed-in owner submits a name (whitespace normalised, 3-40 characters, letters required, no links or markup). The server refuses a name that already exists in the catalog exactly or nearly (case, spacing, punctuation, a Gaming / Game / Esports prefix, plural), the same user's pending suggestion of the same name, and more than 5 suggestions in 24 hours. A suggestion is stored with its user, name, time and status PENDING, and the owner sees a confirmation and their recent suggestions. A suggestion is never a role until an administrator approves it.

Administrators are a server-side list (private.gamid_admins; on TESTING the owner account of @black); no client flag is trusted. They are notified of each suggestion through GamID Notifications (role.suggestion_submitted) and review pending suggestions in an admin-only Role Suggestions block at the very end of the Profile Editor's Gaming Roles section, after Suggest a Role (built only when the server says the account is an administrator; there is no separate Role Suggestions card; its actions are immediate and never part of the Gaming Roles draft or its Save): Approve assigns one of the eight categories and an optional final name (refused if it would duplicate a role) and makes the role selectable in the catalog at once, resolving other pending suggestions of the same name; Reject closes it. The submitter is notified of the decision (role.suggestion_approved / role.suggestion_rejected).

capabilities.name: Mobile Intro landscape rotation hint

contracts.rule: The shared Intro player (account/intro-preview.html: the public visitor Intro and the editor Preview Intro) shows a small animated phone turning from portrait to landscape, bottom-left above the progress bar, once per presentation and only after metadata shows a landscape video (width / height of at least 1.2) on a touch-first (coarse pointer) screen held in portrait. It is never shown for portrait or square videos, before metadata, in landscape or on Desktop. It stays about 6 s: fully visible for 5.5 s, then a 0.5 s fade during which it is still tappable, gone at 6 s (Mazen 2026-10-17). It never loops, never covers the Play button (Play Intro), Skip, the progress bar or the host controls, and is static with reduced motion.

Tapping the hint puts the existing Intro layer (same video, ambient background and controls) in fullscreen, then tries a landscape orientation lock where the browser grants it; a refused lock keeps fullscreen and manual rotation. It never plays, pauses, seeks, reloads or replaces the video: a paused Intro stays paused until Play, and a playing one keeps its position, volume and mute. Exit fullscreen, system Back, Skip, a stop and the Intro end leave fullscreen and release the lock; the end transition runs after fullscreen has closed. Without the Fullscreen API the hint is only a manual-rotation cue. Intro remains click-to-play; the Intro iframes allow fullscreen. The browser's own fullscreen notice (e.g. Chrome's "To exit full screen, press Esc") belongs to the browser and cannot be suppressed by the site; fullscreen is entered only on an explicit tap.

Every sticker waits for the Wall owner's approval; pending and rejected stickers (and their links) are never shown to anyone else. The owner sees the sticker, the sender's avatar and @username, the stage and the clip link before deciding, and approves or rejects the whole submission. A request whose Friends Stage is no longer on the owner's Wall can only be rejected. The owner can remove an approved sticker (asked once, permanent) and drag it on its Friends Stage (desktop and touch); a saved move notifies the sender once. Each newly approved sticker starts at 100%; every newer active approved sticker on the same Wall takes 5 percentage points off an older one, never below 50% (size = max(50, 100 - 5 x newer)). Approvals on one Wall are numbered in a stable order, also under concurrent approvals; pending, rejected and removed stickers never count.

capabilities.name: Custom Wall fonts (Upload My Font / My Fonts)

contracts.rule: An owner uploads a WOFF2, TTF or OTF font in the desktop Text panel (Upload My Font, 900px and wider) after confirming they own it or are licensed to embed it on the web. Only the usage-upload gateway stores it, and it tells the formats apart by their bytes, never by the extension or declared type. A WOFF2 (at most 2 MiB) must pass the structural WOFF2 check. A TTF / OTF (at most 8 MiB; collections and WOFF 1 refused) must pass a structural sfnt check and is converted on the server to WOFF2 by repackaging its tables unchanged (WOFF2 null transform, the runtime's Brotli) - no font program is executed. Only the resulting validated WOFF2 is stored, at most 2 MiB, named by its own SHA-256; the source is never stored.

At most 3 custom fonts per account at a time (stored fonts, not lifetime uploads), enforced by the database at quota reservation and again at registration under the per-account lock, counting uploads in progress, so concurrent uploads cannot exceed it. A 4th distinct font is refused (WALL_FONT_LIMIT); deleting an unused font frees its slot. Re-uploading an identical font (same SHA-256) is stored once and never takes another slot. No paid extra slots.

Each font belongs only to the uploading account, is never added to the shared GamID library, and its bytes count toward the existing account storage quota (reservation, quota refusal and cleanup rules as for every upload). My Fonts shows n/3; the Usage Center shows Custom Fonts n/3 and Wall Fonts storage.

A text element uses a custom font as fontRef "font:<id>" and keeps its catalog font as the fallback; the editor canvas, Preview and the published Wall all draw it, with the fallback until it loads. A Wall may name only its owner's fonts. Choosing a library font (Text panel or Properties) replaces the custom font.

Fonts are private. A visitor (signed in or not) can read a font only while the published, enabled Wall of a PUBLIC GamID references it; the private font library is never listed or exposed to anyone else.

Deleting a font follows the universal deletion rule (wall-universal-delete): every deletion is confirmed first - simply when the font is unused (it then frees its slot); a font in use gets the detailed confirmation that the text's appearance will change, then is deleted and removed from the saved and published Wall, each text falling back to its library font. IN USE: the detailed confirmation shows its name, where it is used, what deleting it does and the effect on the published Wall, with Cancel / Delete. Cancel is the default and Escape cancels. Confirm: it is deleted and every reference to it is resolved. Cancel: nothing changes. Stage deletion keeps its own confirmation (wall-editor-stages-bar); removing an element from the canvas is unchanged and undoable.

A confirmed media deletion removes, in one database transaction, the Whole Wall background, every stage background and every element that uses the file - in the saved draft (only at the revision the editor holds) and in the published Wall - then deletes the asset; nothing else on the Wall changes. capabilities.name: Game artwork from SteamGridDB on TESTING (all accounts; provisional)

contracts.rule: On TESTING, game artwork from SteamGridDB is enabled for every account the same way (no per-account restriction; Mazen's product-owner decision 2026-10-11). It is active only while the server secret STEAMGRIDDB_API_KEY is set and the TESTING-wide artwork switch is ON; switching it off hides every image at once and loses no user data (only a metadata cache of provider ids and image URLs is kept, 7 days; no image is stored or re-served). SteamGridDB's Terms of Use allow personal, non-commercial use and require its explicit written permission for distribution; that permission has not been obtained, so no Production / public / commercial release.

For ordinary visitors, only games the visitor can already see get artwork (public My Games, a public League account, the public crews section, the game of a published Crew Wall). A game is matched by its catalog Steam app id, or else only when exactly one provider title equals the catalog title and the release years agree; anything else keeps the initials tile. Images are static and non-NSFW, load from the provider CDN with no referrer, and the provider key never reaches the browser.

On TESTING, Desktop Account My Games and authenticated saved Classic owner preview reuse the existing artwork resolver, CDN image renderer, strict matching and metadata cache through GET game-artwork/owner/self. Caller-scoped owner RPCs establish identity and canonical manual/discovered library keys; existing eligible public Classic targets for that same owner are retained. URL handles or browser game keys cannot select private data. Canonical catalog metadata is read for at most 64 derived targets, with existing six-lookup request budget, 30-request rate limit, seven-day cache and TESTING kill switch. Responses are private/no-store and vary by authorization. Anonymous/invalid sessions cannot read private targets; ordinary public Classic and Crew visibility gates remain unchanged. No game-account discovery/refresh, profile mutation, database migration or new media service is performed.

capabilities.name: Edit Crew Name (the owner renames a Crew from My Crew)

contracts.rule: In My Crew, the Crew owner sees a pencil beside the Crew name. It opens an inline field with the current name and Save / Cancel. Save shows a saving state and accepts one request at a time; a failure stays visible inline until the owner edits the name or cancels; success shows the new name at once. Members and invitees cannot rename, and the server refuses anyone but the owner (CREW_OWNER_ONLY).

The new name is trimmed and follows the Crew creation rule: 2-40 characters, no control characters, no < or >; empty or whitespace-only names are refused (INVALID_CREW_NAME). Crew names have no uniqueness rule.

A rename changes only the Crew's name. Its id, game, owner, members, invitations, membership status, Crew Wall (stages, member cards, published state) and URLs are unchanged; the Crew is never recreated. Every display reads the name live (My Crew, the public My Crews / Crews sections, the Crew Wall), and members' open pages are told to re-read. The game and owner stay immutable.
